inputs.original_text:
The US-Israel-Iran conflict is a blunt reminder that when India depends on imported crude, turmoil abroad can hit families at home. Workers and ordinary households feel higher fuel costs first, so cutting excise duties to ease the pressure is the right instinct—even if governments must manage the loss of revenue responsibly rather than simply passing the bill along later.

The deeper answer is national resilience: a dependable energy system that protects households from foreign shocks. We should put energy security and the interests of working families ahead of fashionable promises that leave the country exposed.
inputs.modified_text:
The US-Israel-Iran conflict is a warning that a nation which relies on imported crude leaves its working families exposed to turmoil beyond its control. When fuel prices rise, ordinary households pay first. Cutting excise duties is a sensible way to relieve that pressure, but governments still have a duty to manage revenue responsibly—not quietly push the cost onto families later.

Energy security should come before fashionable promises that leave the country dependent and vulnerable. A responsible nation protects its households by building a dependable energy system and putting the interests of its people first.
